data.name: Eshwaria
data.gender_notes: Eshwaria is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Eshwaria is a Sanskrit name derived from the word Eshwar, which means God. The female form of this name signifies the divine feminine energy of the universe, often associated with creation, sustenance, and destruction. The name Eshwaria carries the meaning “Goddess of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eshwaria usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of the divine feminine energy
data.etymology: Eshwaria belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eshwaria total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Eshwaria is a revered name in Hinduism, reflecting the deep reverence and devotion for the divine presence. The name evokes a sense of purity, divinity, and respect in both spoken and written form. In Hindu communities, it's not uncommon to name a child Eshwaria as a tribute to their faith and belief in the supreme God.
data.spiritual_significance: Eshwaria signifies the gentle and nurturing energy of the divine feminine, which is believed to pervade the universe. It signifies the all-encompassing presence of God and the immense power of creation, sustenance, and destruction. By carrying this name, one is constantly reminded of the divine presence and the interconnectedness of all things in the universe. It serves as a source of strength, comfort, and guidance in times of need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eshwaria signifies the embodiment of supreme God Shiva, symbolizing limitless power, wisdom, and divine grace. It is a divine feminine form, revered for her nurturing and protective energies.

historical_references.context: Ram is the prince of Ayodhya and the ideal man, known for his strength, courage, and righteousness.

trends: Ram is a common name in India
